correctness.rationale: The two explicit edge sets are connected ten-edge graphs on eleven vertices and hence trees. Clique complexes of trees equal the trees; therefore the independence complexes of their complements are the trees. The forest/root enumeration reconstructs all acyclic matchings, yielding \(z_1^{-1}\det(z_0z_1 I+L)\) and no missing critical-cell normalization. An exact Newton-identity checker and independent \(2^{10}\) weighted-forest census give a shared Laplacian characteristic polynomial (1,-20,169,-788,2223,-3916,4295,-2838,1051,-188,11,0). Exact \(2^{10}\) matching-mask enumerations give (1,10,34,46,23,2) and (1,10,34,46,23,3). The partition-into-tree-cliques formula for coloring complements yields \(\chi(G_B;q)-\chi(G_A;q)=(q)_6\); independent backtracking verifies six-coloring counts 1440 and 2160. All quantifiers and graph conventions are explicit. The proof does not infer an infinite claim from finite tests.

value.rationale: Zheng explicitly asks whether the independence Morse-ensemble polynomial determines chromatic polynomials. The negative witness is a precise boundary on that new topological-combinatorial invariant: even with contractible one-dimensional independence complexes, a *complete* distribution of Morse critical vectors misses the number of optimal six-colorings. This is a motivated response to a named open structural question, not a data-table recomputation for its own sake. The finite witness and its exact polynomial identity have interpretable mathematical consequences without claiming an unproved general classification.
